arxiv-2109-13570.title: Adaptive Informative Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV-based Active Sensing
arxiv-2109-13570.creator: Julius Rückin, Liren Jin, Marija Popović
arxiv-2109-13570.description: Abstract Aerial robots are increasingly being utilized for environmental monitoring and exploration. However, a key challenge is efficiently planning paths to maximize the information value of acquired data as an initially unknown environment is explored. To address this, we propose a new approach for informative path planning based on deep reinforcement learning (RL).

arxiv-2302-00229.description: Abstract Gravitational waves offer a new window to probe the nature of gravity, including answering if the mediating particle, graviton, has a non-zero mass or not. Pulsar timing arrays measure stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) at ∼ 1 − 100 \sim 1-100 nanohertz.

arxiv-2503-10227.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. Hrmo, S. Kováčik, P. Rusnák, J. Tekel. The fuzzy onion model formed by connecting a set of concentric fuzzy spheres of increasing radius is motivated by studies of quantum space but can also be used to study standard physics. arxiv-2508-10336.creator: Humbert, P, Gazin, U, Heller, R, Roquain, E
arxiv-2508-10336.description: Abstract In a supervised online setting, quantifying uncertainty has been proposed in the seminal work of Gibbs and Candes, 2021 . For any given point-prediction algorithm, their method (ACI) produces a conformal prediction set with an average missed coverage getting close to a pre-specified level α \alpha for a long time horizon.

arxiv-2511-04201.description: Abstract We introduce the concept of compact quantitative equational theory. A quantitative equational theory is defined to be compact if all its consequences are derivable by means of finite proofs. We prove that the theory of interpolative barycentric (also known as convex) quantitative algebras of Mardare et. al. is compact.

pmc-11509391.title: Response of a Blood Clot Adherent to Bone, Oral Mucosa and Hard Dental Tissues to a Uniaxial Tensile Test: An In Vitro Study
pmc-11509391.creator: Gaia Pellegrini, Roberto Fedele, Daniela Carmagnola, Claudia Dellavia, Giorgio Pagni, Dolaji Henin, Gianguido Cossellu, Sabrine Fessi, Giulio Rasperini, Bruno Chrcanovic
pmc-11509391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and Objectives: Periodontal therapy aims to arrest the progression of periodontal diseases and possibly to regenerate the periodontal apparatus. To shift healing from repair to regeneration, the blood clot that fills the periodontal defect and remains in contact with structures such as tooth root, mucosa and bone needs to be stable, which is a reason why the treatment of non-containing periodontal bone defects, in which the clot may undergo displacement, is challenging.

pmc-12402075.title: M-estimation activation functions for high-performance extreme learning machine ensemble classification
pmc-12402075.creator: Fathi Alimi, Adnan Khan, Hameed Ali, Mohamed Bouzidi, Abdulrahman Obaid Alshammari, Bakhtiyar Ahmad
pmc-12402075.description: Machine learning plays a pivotal role in addressing real-world challenges across domains such as cybersecurity, where AI-driven methods, especially in Software-Defined Networking, enhance traffic monitoring and anomaly detection. Contemporary networks often employ models like Random Forests, Neural Networks, and Support Vector Machines to identify threats early and reinforce security.

pmc-12430863.title: Litchi LcAP1-1 and LcAP1-2 Exhibit Different Roles in Flowering Time
pmc-12430863.creator: Qiulin Gui, Jinju Wei, Ziang Wu, Xiao Mo, Haowei Qing, Yuyu Shi, Huiqin Guo, Jingwen Sheng, Feng Ding, Shuwei Zhang, Jiangqi Wen
pmc-12430863.description: Litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.) is a kind of evergreen fruit tree with good flavor and taste which has high economic value. Sufficiently low temperature in winter is essential for the successful flower formation of litchi. Therefore, in the context of global warming, litchi often experiences unstable flower formation, ultimately resulting in a decrease in litchi production.

pmc-12656065.title: Relationship Between Internal and External Load in Under-16 Soccer Players: Heart Rate, Rating of Perceived Exertion, and GPS-Derived Variables
pmc-12656065.creator: Krisztián Havanecz, Sándor Sáfár, Csaba Bartha, Bence Kopper, Tamás Horváth, Péter János Tóth, Gabriella P Szabó, Zoltán Szalánczi, Gábor Géczi, Luís Branquinho, Corrado Lupo
pmc-12656065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Heart rate (HR) monitoring is a practical method for assessing internal load (IL). However, it remains unclear for which age group HR would be an appropriate predictor of IL considering the relationship with external load (EL). Thus, this study aims to evaluate the relevance and applicability of HR monitoring by exploring the relationship between EL and IL among U16 soccer players.

pmc-12719849.title: Mid‐term survival in patients awaiting heart and kidney transplantation with Impella 5.5 support
pmc-12719849.creator: Smruti Desai, Smit Paghdar, Jose Ruiz, Ji‐Min Jang, Sharan Malkani, Daniel S Yip, Juan Leoni, Jose Nativi, Basar Sareyyupoglu, Kevin Landolfo, Si Pham, Parag Patel, Rohan Goswami
pmc-12719849.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPatients with end‐stage heart failure and chronic kidney disease requiring dual‐organ transplantation (DOT) face significant challenges in utilizing durable mechanical circulatory support due to the risks associated with renal replacement therapies (RRTs) and multi‐organ failure. Given the limited options available for long‐term support in this patient population, there remains a critical need for alternative strategies to optimize end‐organ function and bridge patients safely to transplant.

pmc-12749354.title: Over-reliance on short-acting beta-agonists (SABAs) in asthma: a mixed method study, in primary care, in Greece
pmc-12749354.creator: Izolde Bouloukaki, Antonios Christodoulakis, Siân Williams, Ioanna Tsiligianni
pmc-12749354.description: IntroductionOver-reliance on short-acting beta-agonists (SABAs) has been identified as a predictor of poor asthma control and increased asthma-related mortality. The aim of the study was to assess SABA over-reliance and its association with asthma control and the utility of the Reliever Reliance Test (RRT) in addressing SABA over-reliance in primary care patients.

pmc-13010622.title: A Multidisciplinary Approach to the Diagnosis and Management of a Mammary Myofibroblastoma in a Male with a History of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report
pmc-13010622.creator: Carmen Montes Fernández, Norma C. Gutiérrez, Elena Alejo Alonso, Susana Gallego García, Luis Gonzaga Díaz-González, José Luis Revilla Hernández, María Ángeles Hernández García, Idalia González Morais, Miguel Ángel Cruz Sánchez, José María Sayagués, Luis Miguel Chinchilla-Tábora
pmc-13010622.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Clinical Significance: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is a morphologically and molecularly heterogeneous lymphoproliferative disorder that originates from a clonal B-cell ancestor. Patients usually present with rapidly enlarging lymph nodes or mass(es) at single or multiple sites. Generally, 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography with computed tomography (PET-CT) is performed post-treatment to evaluate remission status, especially in radiologically residual tumors. Myofibroblastoma (MFB) is a benign mesenchymal tumor of the mammary stroma composed of fibroblasts and myofibroblasts.

pmc-13179695.title: Chest Compressions as a Precipitant of Aortocaval Hematoma and Pseudoaneurysm in the Setting of Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) Filter Aortic Penetration: A Case Report
pmc-13179695.creator: Anthony N Cholagh, Deema Ujayli, Ragamayi Maramraju, Mansi Joglekar, Rohan Patel
pmc-13179695.description: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are associated with delayed complications, including aortic penetration, which may present asymptomatically or with clinical sequelae warranting vascular intervention. We present a case of a 52-year-old male with a known indwelling IVC filter with aortic penetration who developed an aortocaval hematoma and pseudoaneurysm following a brief resuscitative event involving chest compressions.

pmc-13185920.title: Contextual fear conditioning leads to hypo-innervation of the left ventricular myocardium in female but not male C57BL/6J mice
pmc-13185920.creator: Luca M Lautenschläger, Lara Mariel Chirich Barreira, Jonas Labode, Julia Schipke, Anne Albrecht, Christian Mühlfeld
pmc-13185920.description: ObjectiveContextual fear conditioning is an effective way of inducing and modelling anxiety-like states in rodents like mice. We examined the sex-dependent effects of contextual fear conditioning on the autonomic innervation of the left ventricular myocardium in female and male mice.

pmc-13196050.title: Schisandrin B alleviates high-glucose diet-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and tissue injury in zebrafish and is associated with alterations in intestinal microbiota
pmc-13196050.creator: Miao Fu, Wei Xu, Changmin Deng, Anhuai Yang, Mingyang Xue, Xuan Xiao, Lijuan Xu
pmc-13196050.description: High-glucose diet (HGD) has been reported to alter gut microbiota and induce chronic inflammation and oxidative stress. In this study, we demonstrated that Schisandrin B (SchB) markedly attenuated HGD-induced physiological disturbances in zebrafish, with a focus on multiple tissues, including the liver, intestine, brain, and retina.

pmc-13389027.title: Rabies virus glycoprotein variants modulate neuronal nicotinic receptors in a conformation-dependent manner
pmc-13389027.creator: Seyedeh Melika Akaberi, Sabina Yeasmin, Pooja Sapkota, Kavita Sharma, Marvin Schulte
pmc-13389027.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rabies encephalitis remains nearly 100% fatal once symptoms appear, and no effective treatments exist because the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal disruption remain poorly understood. This has prevented the development of molecular-based therapies, leaving only symptomatic management strategies. RABV-G has long been proposed to interact with muscle and, more recently, neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), but neuronal receptors have only been implicated using short peptide fragments.

pmc-13427884.title: AML with t(16;21)(p11.2;q22)/FUS::ERG rearrangement presenting with hemophagocytes and multinucleated cells: a case report and literature review
pmc-13427884.creator: Yingying Chen, XinhongYang, Zhihua Zhang, Xiaofeng Yang
pmc-13427884.description: The FUS::ERG fusion gene is rare in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), with a predominant prevalence in individuals of Asian descent. The incidence of AML harboring the FUS::ERG fusion gene is approximately 1%.Including the present case, a total of 154 cases have been reported in the literature to date.
